subject: Inference cost precision: pilot outline, decision criteria & budget confirmation
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Inference cost precision: pilot outline, decision criteria & budget confirmation

John / Lori — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposal so we have shared next steps. I captured the pain, goals, cost levers we discussed and a proposed pilot that lets us validate economics and latency risk before a larger commitment. Please review and tell us if any of this misses the mark.

Pain points you confirmed
- Token volume growth from user search and summarization flows causing unpredictable spend month-to-month.
- P95 latency spikes on peak traffic (search) that impact conversion.
- Procurement requires a clear pilot ROI and defined decision criteria before internal approvals.

Primary goals for a pilot
- Demonstrate >30% reduction in per-token inference cost versus your current endpoint through batching/caching/quantization without degrading p95 latency beyond 20% of baseline.
- Validate routing/fallback so production SLOs aren't violated during model/size experiments.
- Produce a reproducible cost model that your procurement team can review.

Proposed pilot (3-week technical pilot) — scope highlights
- Workloads: generation for search snippets (~70% traffic) + embeddings for similarity (~30%).
- Traffic target: average 0.8–1.2M tokens/day; peak bursts up to 4M/day for 2–3 hours.
- Success metrics: per-1k-token cost delta, p95 latency (target <300ms for search snippet path), cache hit rate >= 25% for prefix caching.
- Levers we'll explore: (1) request-level continuous batching (dynamic batch sizes tuned by p95 budget), (2) prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, (3) quantization profiles (4-bit/8-bit) for embeddings pipeline.

Initial cost framing (ballpark)
- Baseline: your existing provider estimate baked to ~ $12,000–$15,000 / week for the observed volume.
- Pilot target: implement batching + caching + quantization to target a 30–50% reduction in unit cost. That implies ~ $6,000–$10,500 / week during pilot depending on config.
- We'll deliver a model-level scatter of cost vs latency so procurement sees tradeoffs explicitly. I attached a short pricing snapshot and the proposed pilot scope doc.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Confirm budget range for an exploratory pilot (you mentioned ~ $60k/quarter as an upper bound; confirm if pilot funding comes from that headroom).
2) Confirm procurement contact and preferred contracting cadence — we can provide an SOW and a short 1-page MSA addendum.
3) Approve kickoff window: earliest options are Tue 11/16 or Wed 11/17 for a 60m technical kickoff with your eng/infra folks.
4) Share a test dataset or representative prompt set (or grant read-only S3 access) for realistic cache-hit tuning.

Attachments: redwood-pilot-scope-v1.pdf, acme-pricing-snapshot.xlsx

Thanks — I looped Rishi and Dev for technical follow-ups. If the team wants, we can also run a quick cost-sensitivity table during the kickoff to lock in the decision criteria procurement needs.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Stephanie — clear note and helpful framing. A few quick items from our side:
- Budget: the $60k/quarter is a general cap; for a short 3-week exploratory pilot we can commit up to $25k as long as we have clear acceptance criteria and an easy opt-out. Procurement needs a 1-page cost justification.
- Latency risk: we need a clearer breakdown of how each lever (batching vs caching vs quantization) impacts p95 latency. If caching helps cost but risks p95 on cold starts, we need to quantify that.
- Timeline: procurement has a tight window — we'd like a signed SOW by 11/24 to include in Q4 vendor list.

Can Rishi or Dev provide a short table of expected p95 impact (estimated) per lever? Also cc'ing procurement to keep them in the loop.

On availability: Wed 11/17 for kickoff works for us.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Inference cost precision: pilot outline, decision criteria & budget confirmation (technical notes)

Stephanie — quick tech notes to attach to the SOW and to prepare for the kickoff. Keep these high level for procurement and save deeper details for the technical session.

Summary of expected impacts (rough estimates, will validate during pilot):
- Continuous batching (adaptive batching to p95 budget): expected unit cost reduction 20–35% depending on traffic parallelism; p95 latency impact: +10–25% under peak if batch windows exceed 10–20ms; mitigations: dynamic max-batch and latency SLO-driven cutoff.
- Prefix / KV caching: hit-rate dependent — with a 25–30% prefix hit rate we expect 15–30% cost reduction on generation path; p95 impact negligible for warm hits, but cold-starts can introduce 50–150ms extra due to cache-warm flows; mitigation: proactive pre-warming for planned bursts.
- Quantization (4-bit for embeddings, 8-bit for generation where applicable): embeddings cost per token can drop ~30–45% with negligible quality regression for retrieval; generation quantization needs evaluation for quality-sensitive prompts — start with hybrid where embeddings use 4-bit and generation uses 8-bit.

Estimated unit economics (pilot baseline assumptions):
- Baseline unit: $0.016 per 1k tokens (rounded from current vendor estimate)
- Post-levers target range: $0.008–$0.011 per 1k tokens (combined batching + caching + quant)
- For 1M tokens/day: baseline ~$16/day -> target ~$8–$11/day (wide band; will refine with logs).

Attachments to prepare for kickoff: short runbook for performance tuning, example cache key design, quantization test checklist. I'll assemble these into a single tech appendix.

Rishi
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Pilot budget request: $18k–$25k for the 3-week technical pilot (covers reserved test capacity, engineering hours, and telemetry instrumentation). This fits within your $25k pilot commit and leaves room for optional add-on tests (e.g., cache pre-warm).
- SOW and approval: I’ve prepared a short SOW and DocuSign link here: https://docusign.com/s/ACME-SOW-059 (draft). If procurement can review and sign by 11/24 we can start kickoff 11/17 and finish the validation window before month-end.

2) John/Lori: approve the 11/17 kickoff or propose an alternate time.
3) Technical: Dev/Rishi will need read-only access to a representative prompt set or an S3 path by 11/13 to build cache keys and baseline metrics.

I'll update HubSpot and drop the SOW into DocuSign for signatures after we get procurement's path. If useful, happy to run a short 15-minute pre-kickoff call with procurement to walk the cost table.
